what_it_does: This paper addresses wearable medical imaging using photoacoustic imaging—a technique where a laser pulse excites tissue and the resulting acoustic waves are detected to form an image of internal structures. The challenge is that photoacoustic signals are very weak (ten times smaller than ultrasound) and wearable devices need to stream data efficiently. The authors integrate data compression directly into the analog-to-digital converter using a technique called 'matrix multiplication SAR.' The converter simultaneously acquires the weak photoacoustic signal and performs a mathematical operation (multiplying the signal by a carefully chosen pattern) that compresses it on the fly. This reduces data volume without losing critical signal information and minimizes power consumption in the sensor.
